item.title: Critical Decisions Shape AI's Future
item.description:
The Turbulent AI Era Is Here: Why Our Choices Matter Now More Than Ever

We stand at an inflection point in human technological history. Artificial intelligence has moved from academic laboratories and specialized applications into mainstream consciousness and everyday use. Yet unlike previous technological revolutions that unfolded over decades, the AI transformation is happening at breathtaking speed. This acceleration creates both unprecedented opportunities and significant risks—and the decisions we make in this critical window will reverberate for generations.
item.tweet: AI's trajectory isn't predetermined. The choices we make now—about safety, governance, access, and equity—will echo for decades. item.title: Gates Warns Turbulent AI Era Arrives
item.description:
Gates Warns Turbulent AI Era Arrives

Bill Gates published a new Gates Notes essay arguing that the turbulent AI era is already here and that near-term choices will decide whether benefits outweigh harms. The piece, framed as an “epochal shift,” does not treat artificial intelligence as a distant forecast or as science fiction waiting on some future breakthrough. It treats the present as the period that matters. That framing, and the call for a concrete plan so AI works for everyone rather than concentrating upside or accelerating downside risks, is what carried the essay to the top of Google News technology and AI last-hour feeds on Saturday night.

item.title: Socket Sensor Warns Before Tissue Injury
item.description:
Socket Sensor Warns Before Tissue Injury

A prosthetic socket is a tight, load-bearing cup. For someone who walks on a residual limb, that cup is also a risk. Pressure that lasts too long, or that concentrates on the wrong patch of skin, can injure tissue that has already been through amputation, healing, and the daily friction of a liner. Researchers at Zhejiang University of Technology built a bioinspired sensor layer meant to sit inside a prosthetic socket and flag pressure that can injure residual-limb skin, ScienceAlert reported from a Cyborg and Bionic Systems study.

item.title: Abbott freezes Texas Flock camera funding
item.description:
Abbott freezes Texas Flock camera funding

Texas Gov. Greg Abbott ordered state agencies to pause funding for Flock Safety’s AI-powered license-plate cameras as privacy backlash and alleged police misuse spread. The Texas Tribune said the order came as it prepared an investigation showing a state agency had put at least $30 million into the Flock network via local-police grants.

A pause is not a ban. It is a governor hitting freeze on a network that can already see a lot of Texas asphalt. Spokesman Andrew Mahaleris said most city camera money is federal, and Texas agencies are clarifying that state funds cannot be used for Flock. That split is the whole fight: who paid, who can look, and who gets to keep looking while Austin pretends the tap is off.

item.title: Activision Serves Cheat Seller On Camera
item.description:
Activision Serves Cheat Seller On Camera

The knock came with a camera. At 9:50 a.m. on August 22, during the Modern Warfare 4 closed beta, a process server stood at an Ohio house and handed Elocarry, a well-known cheat vendor, a cease-and-desist. Call of Duty’s official X account posted the one-minute clip the same day. The framing was not subtle. This was a live RICOCHET takedown. The caption might as well have been a slogan on a crate: “Cheat makers operate around the world. So do we.”

item.title: Apple Jacks Up Streaming Prices Again
item.description:
Apple Jacks Up Streaming Prices Again

Apple has never liked looking cheap. It likes looking worth it. That distinction is how a company can charge more for a phone and call it taste. It is also how a company can raise a streaming bill for the fourth time in the United States and still insist, with a straight face, that the service is a bargain.

Ars Technica, citing Variety, reported the latest turn of that logic. Apple raised U.S. Apple TV by $2 a month to $15, and lifted the annual plan 20 percent, from $99 to $119. New sign-ups pay immediately. Existing customers get about a month’s notice. The increase is small enough to sound like a rounding error and large enough, in the history of this particular product, to complete a tripling.

item.title: GTA 6 Crashes Twitch and Netflix
item.description:
GTA 6 Crashes Twitch and Netflix

For more than a decade, Grand Theft Auto has been less a video game than a civic event that happens to ship on a disc. When Rockstar finally showed the first real GTA 6 gameplay, the internet treated it that way. The company did not put the footage on its own channel first. It put it on Netflix, as a Netflix-exclusive Extended Look, and then watched half the living room of the internet try to squeeze through the same door.
